number.why: The primary MACE result is alirocumab versus placebo HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.78–0.93. The registry confirms ITT and the full study window up to 64 months; the abstract reports median follow-up of 2.8 years. The endpoint includes unstable angina requiring hospitalization, consistent with the served broad MACE outcome.

quotes.span: A composite primary end-point event occurred in 903 patients (9.5%) in the alirocumab group and in 1052 patients (11.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 0.93; P<0.001).
The primary end point was a composite of death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, fatal or nonfatal ischemic stroke, or unstable angina requiring hospitalization.
TIME FRAME: From randomization up to 64 months | POPULATION: Intent-to-treat (ITT) population included all randomized participants.
The median duration of follow-up was 2.8 years.
RESULT OUTCOME 0 ANALYSIS 0: groups Placebo, Alirocumab 75 mg Q2W/Up to 150 mg Q2W | Hazard Ratio (HR) 0.85 (95% CI 0.78 to 0.93) | p 0.0003 | METHOD Log Rank |

entry.why: Eligibility establishes adults with ASCVD following recent ACS, and the trial directly compares alirocumab with placebo using randomized, double-blind allocation.

quotes.span: ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 40 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL
We conducted a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 18,924 patients who had an acute coronary syndrome 1 to 12 months earlier
Patients were randomly assigned to receive alirocumab subcutaneously at a dose of 75 mg (9462 patients) or matching placebo (9462 patients) every 2 weeks.

missed: No omission changes either ruling. The cross-source metadata overlooks the registry's directly reported HR and CI, quoted above, which independently corroborate the served estimate rather than merely providing a percentage ratio.
